# DEV-01 — Create the application skeleton and deterministic demo environment

BANK-S02-v0.4 · Detailed specification candidate; implementation not started.
Forecast: S02 | Release: B0 | Estimate: Dev 3, BA 0.25, QA 0.5 person-days. Provisional until technical review.

## Business purpose and scope

As a contributor, I want a repeatable local environment so that I can develop and review the manual service workflow without a model key.

Value: Provide reproducible engineering evidence while keeping domain decisions visible. Owner relevance: customer-service desktop, banking product/BA and prior frontend experience. Target-role evidence: repository R01/R02/R06 requirements/API/testing/enterprise delivery samples; no new vacancy or proficiency claim.

No business story marked complete just because services start. All operational scenarios and records are synthetic.

Requirements: FR-12, DATA-01. Dependencies: BA-07, BA-08, BA-09.

## Delivery flow

1. Create React/TypeScript UI, FastAPI service, PostgreSQL migration setup and health/readiness endpoints.
2. Add isolated synthetic seed/reset command, configuration validation and safe .env.example.
3. Keep Python 3.9 evaluation modules separate from Python 3.12 application dependencies; lock versions after compatibility checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-01-AC01** — Given A clean supported checkout with empty demo database; when run documented migration and seed commands twice; then second run changes no fixture IDs or counts; API and UI display labelled synthetic scenario and schema version. Evidence: DEV-01-T01, planned/not executed.
- **DEV-01-AC02** — Given No model credentials; when start UI/API/worker and complete manual lookup; then manual path remains usable; agent availability is explicitly disabled. Evidence: DEV-01-T02, planned/not executed.
- **DEV-01-AC03** — Given Database is unavailable or a required configuration value is malformed; when check liveness and readiness; then process liveness is separate from dependency readiness; readiness is non-success with sanitized correlation ID. Evidence: DEV-01-T03, planned/not executed.
- **DEV-01-AC04** — Given Reset is aimed at a database not explicitly marked disposable demo; when request reset; then refuse without deleting records; reset requires matching environment guard and explicit demo target. Evidence: DEV-01-T04, planned/not executed.
- **DEV-01-AC05** — Given Repository existing Python 3.9 evaluation suite; when install Python 3.12 application dependencies in separate environment; then legacy suite remains independently runnable; app lock and setup record supported versions. Evidence: DEV-01-T05, planned/not executed.

## Ready and Done boundaries

Ready requires versioned technical contract/fixtures, validated dependencies and a story walkthrough. Business rules D-17–D-22 are accepted; proposed business-benefit targets and model budgets are not silently approved. Platform stories can proceed against explicitly frozen draft contracts; dependent workflow acceptance requires those contracts implemented. Done requires the listed tests and review evidence, not merely this document.

Design (repository: design.md) · Tasks (repository: tasks.md) · Acceptance (repository: acceptance.md) · Current contracts (repository: ../contracts/interface-notes.md)

## Components and contracts

apps/web (React/TypeScript), services/api (FastAPI/Python 3.12), worker entrypoint, PostgreSQL and migrations form one Compose development boundary. Version locks follow a compatibility smoke run; none is claimed installed by this spec. /health/live reports process life; /health/ready reports database/schema readiness without credentials. Configuration loads server-side; fake identity adapter uses fixed synthetic principals and cannot be enabled in public mode.

## State, exceptions and evidence

Named seed fixtures: posted plus pending pair, two posted equal amounts without proof, reversed charge, missing merchant context and forbidden second customer. Seed/reset requires disposable-demo database marker, not merely an environment-name string.

Shared invariants: server-derived identity/assignment; source and record versions; typed safe errors; idempotent command receipts; no model approval/financial authority; database business/audit/outbox atomicity. Trace only sanitized IDs, versions, outcome, latency and usage provenance. Customer content is untrusted input.

## Delivery and recovery

Runnable skeleton, migrations, seed tooling, environment guide and architecture ADR. Reproduce in disposable local/test environment; document exact versions and skipped suites. Runtime/deployment evidence remains pending.

# DEV-02 — Open an authorized contact and assemble permitted customer context

Current S02 forecast: **S03**. Updated effort: Dev 3, BA 0.25, QA 0.5 person-days (3.75 total); dependencies DEV-01, BA-09. This supersedes older forecast/estimate lines below. Contract version 0.4; runtime implementation pending.

Status: Detailed specification candidate; implementation not started. Business decisions accepted only as listed; technical design/Ready gates pending.
Forecast: S03 | Release: B0 manual path / B1 assisted path.
Estimate: Dev 3, BA 0.25, QA 0.5 person-days; total 3.75 (3–6), confidence medium. Not actual effort.

## User story and value

As a ordinary representative, I want a scoped customer and card context, so that I can avoid repeated page navigation without expanding access.

Owner relevance: representative desktop, customer-information lookup and processing-rule experience. Role evidence: requirements/API/access/testing/UAT in dated R01/R02/R06 samples; no current vacancy or outcome claim.

## Scope and authority

Requirements: FR-01, NFR-01. Decisions: D-09, D-11. Dependencies: DEV-01, BA-07, BA-09.
Synthetic records and policies only. Financial execution, real outbound calls, App messaging and a full specialist adjudication platform are excluded.

## Main flow

1. Read identity-verification result and session role from trusted services.
2. Select an authorized card; show masked identifiers, context timestamp and permitted actions.
3. Deny cross-customer reads before model/tool output; retain a manual verification route.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-02-AC01** — Given An authenticated ordinary representative and verified customer context; when the selected card is loaded; then return only the permitted card/account context with source timestamp and version. Evidence: DEV-02-T01 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-02-AC02** — Given An unverified or expired customer context; when any private lookup is requested; then deny without returning private fields and offer the verification route. Evidence: DEV-02-T02 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-02-AC03** — Given A prompt supplies a different customer ID or asks for administrator privileges; when the tool is invoked; then derive scope from the session and disclose no out-of-scope existence or details. Evidence: DEV-02-T03 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-02-AC04** — Given An ordinary representative can read transactions; when a refund or other privileged action is requested; then reject the action; read access does not grant financial authority. Evidence: DEV-02-T04 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-02-AC05** — Given Scope expires between a proposal and approval; when the person attempts to commit; then reject with AUTH_REQUIRED and preserve the editable draft. Evidence: DEV-02-T05 (planned, not executed).

## Ready gates

- Finalize role/action matrix and identity-proofing fixture; no real identity provider is claimed.
- Review data/permission contracts, exact fixtures, dependencies and observable results before moving to Ready.
- No Done status until implementation, appropriate tests, owner UAT and required release evidence exist.

## Traceability

Design (repository: design.md) · Tasks (repository: tasks.md) · Acceptance record (repository: acceptance.md) · Tool contracts (repository: ../contracts/agent-tools.md) · Review increment (repository: ../../docs/sprint-01/workflow-increment.md).


# DEV-02 design

BANK-SDD-v0.2 · Candidate architecture; no runtime implementation.

Model-visible tools: get_contact_context. Human/system commands and complete schemas are in shared contracts (repository: ../contracts/agent-tools.md).

## Delivery boundary

- Persist Contact and server-owned ScopeSnapshot; never accept a model-supplied role.
- Implement scoped context API plus loading/expired/denied states in the workspace.
- Add access tests for representative, specialist and feedback roles; sanitize errors and traces.

## Cross-cutting contract

Backend derives identity and scope. Every returned record carries source/version/as-of. Read, draft and committed states are distinct. No UI-only authorization. Human approval rechecks versions, permissions and allowed transition; commit business data, audit and outbox atomically. Reconcile uncertain outcomes using the operation key. Restart does not lose committed state.

UI must distinguish loading, empty, denied, failed, stale and completed. Manual lookup/edit remains available on agent failure. Show actual receipts and customer-visible explanations separately from internal notes. Tool/schema errors are typed and sanitized; safe correlation IDs link events and evaluation.

## Data and integration

Use explicit foreign keys among contact, case, work item, result, attempt and proposal; version changes must invalidate dependent drafts. Record synthetic provenance. API/data contracts are finalized in BA-07/09 before implementation. Integration tests use a real test database and deterministic calendar, not only model mocks.

## Deployment

Ship through existing API/worker/UI release, with migration and fixture updates. Verify permissions, pending-event replay and rollback/restore in staging before acceptance. This story does not provision infrastructure or contact real customers.

## Main flow

2. For no answer keep feedback ownership and propose the next allowed contact slot.
3. Allow at most three attempts over three service days, including the first; at most one per service date.
4. On exhaustion or elapsed window send to lead review; do not close automatically.
5. On successful feedback allow human-confirmed closure only when all required work is complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-12-AC01** — Given The first actual callback is unanswered; when the retry is planned; then keep awaiting-feedback state and ownership; schedule only within the accepted contact window; under D-18, a placed unanswered call counts once, while a never-placed technical failure is logged without consuming quota or extending any original deadline. - **DEV-12-AC03** — Given Three attempts have been made or the three-service-day window has elapsed; when the next-step rule is evaluated; then enter unable-to-contact lead review with no resolved closure; a responsible lead may then approve a reasoned new contact plan or a hold with owner and review date, retaining original attempts/deadlines/approvals. After contact quota or window exhaustion, the responsible lead may approve a reasoned new contact plan or a review hold with a named owner and review date.
